::: {#exm-normal-normal}
#### Posterior for a Gaussian mean

Suppose that, given the mean $\mu$,
$\dsn{X} \siid \ndist{\mu, 1}$,
so the variance is known,
and that the prior for $\mu$ is $\ndist{0, 1}$.
Let $\vx = (\dsn{x})$ be the observed data,
with sample mean $\bar x$.

The likelihood is

$$
\ba
\p(\vx \mid \mu)
&= \prodin (2\pi)^{-1/2} \expf{-\frac{1}{2}(x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(independent Gaussian observations)}\\
&= (2\pi)^{-n/2} \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\sumin (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(combining the exponents)}\\
&= (2\pi)^{-n/2} \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{\sumin x_i^2 - 2 \mu n \bar x + n \mu^2}}
&& \text{(expanding the square; $\sum_i x_i = n \bar x$)}\\
&\propto \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{n \mu^2 - 2 \mu n \bar x}}
&& \text{(dropping factors that do not involve $\mu$)},
\ea
$$

and the prior density is $\p(\mu) \propto \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\mu^2}$.
Let $m \eqdef \frac{n}{n+1} \bar x$.
By @cor-bayes-proportional,

$$
\ba
\p(\mu \mid \vx)
&\propto \p(\vx \mid \mu)\, \p(\mu)
&& \text{(posterior is proportional to likelihood times prior)}\\
&\propto \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{n \mu^2 - 2 \mu n \bar x}}
  \cdot \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\mu^2}
&& \text{(substituting likelihood and prior)}\\
&= \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{(n+1)\mu^2 - 2 \mu n \bar x}}
&& \text{(adding exponents)}\\
&= \expf{-\frac{1}{2}(n+1)\paren{\mu^2 - 2 \mu m}}
&& \text{(factoring out $n+1$; definition of $m$)}\\
&= \expf{-\frac{1}{2}(n+1)\paren{(\mu - m)^2 - m^2}}
&& \text{(completing the square)}\\
&\propto \expf{-\frac{1}{2}(n+1)(\mu - m)^2}
&& \text{(dropping the factor $\expf{\tfrac{1}{2}(n+1)m^2}$)}.
\ea
$$

The last line is,
up to a constant,
the density of a Gaussian distribution with mean $m$ and variance $1/(n+1)$,
so the posterior is

$$
\mu \mid \vx \;\sim\; \ndist{\frac{n}{n+1}\bar{x},\; \frac{1}{n+1}}.
$$

The posterior mean $\frac{n}{n+1}\bar{x}$ is the sample mean
shrunk toward the prior mean $0$,
and the shrinkage factor $\frac{n}{n+1}$ approaches $1$ as $n \to \infty$.
:::
